title: Quarterly Roadmap Runway: Commitment Sizing and Stakeholder Drift Control for Hosted API + Model Catalog
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Summary:
This ticket defines the quarterly runway and commitment-sizing playbook for the Hosted API + Model Catalog portfolio. The goal is to produce a repeatable decision process that ties OKR-level targets (latency, cost-per-1k-tokens, model coverage) to concrete sprint commitments, canary windows, and contingency lanes for model rotations and capacity shortfalls.

Objectives:
- Produce a 12-week commitment map that matches model onboarding cadence with capacity hedges and rollback policies.
- Define acceptance criteria for swapping hosted model variants (latency delta, quality regression thresholds, cost uplift limits).
- Surface cross-team dependencies and create a simple hedging protocol to avoid over-commitment.
- Deliver a one-page playbook and an associated Confluence runbook with links to simulation dashboards and canary schedules.

Success metrics / OKR alignment:
- Roadmap confidence: reduce unknown-commitment tickets in the next cycle by 40% (PM metric).
- Operational SLOs maintained during rotations: < 2% increase in P50 latency during canaries and < 0.5% error rate delta.
- Cost targets: keep projected per-token cost uplift for new model variants under 12% at commit.

Phases & deliverables:
1) Discovery (Week 1-2): collect historical canary outcomes, cost deltas, and token distribution data. Deliverable: Data snapshot + simulation notebook (Drive link).
2) Commitment Sizing (Week 3-4): create sizing rubric that maps expected traffic cohorts to reservation buckets and contingency buffer (burst %). Deliverable: Commitment sizing spreadsheet and template.
3) Playbook & Escalation (Week 5-6): write the one-page playbook covering canary windows, rollback thresholds, and stakeholder notification flows. Deliverable: Confluence playbook + PR template for model swaps.
4) Simulation & Signoff (Week 7-9): run seasonal surge sims with Eng, validate canary thresholds, finalize commit lanes. Deliverable: Simulation dashboard snapshot and signoff doc.
5) Pilot commit (Week 10-12): execute a pilot rotation using the playbook on a non-critical cohort, capture learnings, and iterate. Deliverable: Pilot retro and final playbook v1.

Owners & stakeholders:
- PM lead: Ava Martinez (roadmap coordination, OKR mapping)
- Eng lead: Priya Nair (capacity sims, traffic modeling)
- Design: Marco Lin (console UX for commitment UI)
- Reliability/Oncall: Sophie Keller (SLO verification)
- Solutions/CS: Ben Osei (customer notification cadence)

Acceptance criteria:
- Playbook published in Confluence with explicit canary windows and rollback criteria.
- Commitment sizing template adopted by at least two product teams for next cycle planning.
- Simulation shows < 5% chance of breaching latency SLOs under target surge scenarios.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Model quality regressions discovered late during canary. Mitigation: require a held-back prompt set and automated regression checks before canary expansion.
- Risk: Capacity shortfall during overlapping rotations. Mitigation: define a hard cap on concurrent canaries and an emergency fallback policy to earlier model tier.
- Risk: Stakeholder drift leading to unscoped mid-cycle asks. Mitigation: implement a change request template and triage board (PM gate).

Links & artifacts:
- Confluence draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PM/commitment-sizing-playbook (draft)
- Drive: https://drive.redwood.ai/hostedapi/runway-sims (simulation notebooks)
- GitHub PR template: https://github.com/redwood-inference/hosted-api/pull/placeholder
- Simulation dashboard: internal://dashboards/commitment-sizing-sims (placeholder)

Assumptions:
- Historical token distribution data is accessible to Eng within two working days.
- No major infra changes affecting routing during pilot.

Next steps:
- Triage meeting with Eng & Design scheduled (see updates).
- PM to draft the one-page playbook and circulate for review by Week 4.
